summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2 and node3 (async read-only standbys) on AlmaLinux 9. Verified writes on the primary propagate to both standbys and that standbys reject writes. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes (standbys first, primary last), proving changed boot IDs and confirming full recovery of PostgreSQL, replication streaming, and data on each.
actions_performed: Installed PostgreSQL 16 (module postgresql:16) server/contrib on node1, node2, node3 via dnf
Initialized primary DB on node1 with postgresql-setup --initdb
Configured node1 postgresql.conf: listen_addresses='*', wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders=10, max_replication_slots=10, hot_standby=on
Generated a replication password on node1 itself (openssl rand, stored root-only) and created a REPLICATION LOGIN role 'replicator'
Added pg_hba.conf entries on node1 permitting scram-sha-256 replication connections from node2/node3 IPs, reloaded postgresql
Opened firewalld postgresql service on node1 (initial pg_basebackup attempts failed with 'No route to host' until this was added)
Created a repl_test table with a baseline row on the primary for replication verification
Ran pg_basebackup with -R on node2 and node3 (using secret_env to pass the replication password) to clone the primary and auto-generate standby.signal/primary_conninfo
Started/enabled postgresql on node2 and node3, confirmed pg_is_in_recovery()=true on both and pg_stat_replication shows both streaming (async) on the primary
Verified standbys reject INSERTs (read-only) and that a new INSERT on the primary replicates to both standbys
Captured pre-restart boot_id on all three nodes
Restarted node2 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified postgresql active, in recovery, data intact, and reconnected to primary's replication stream
Restarted node3 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified postgresql active, in recovery, data intact, and reconnected to primary's replication stream

Restarted node1 (primary) via systemctl reboot last (after both standbys were healthy), polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, verified postgresql active, not in recovery, firewall rule persisted, and both standbys reconnected as streaming
Performed a final post-all-restarts INSERT on node1 and confirmed it appeared on both node2 and node3, proving end-to-end replication survived the full restart cycle

evidence.requirement: PostgreSQL streaming replication configured: node1 primary, node2/node3 standbys
evidence.summary: PostgreSQL 16 installed and initialized on node1; replication role, wal_level, pg_hba, and firewall configured; node2/node3 cloned via pg_basebackup -R with standby.signal and primary_conninfo generated, then started.

evidence.requirement: Standbys are streaming and read-only; primary shows both connected replicas
evidence.summary: pg_stat_replication on node1 lists both node2 and node3 in 'streaming' state; pg_is_in_recovery() is true on both standbys; an INSERT attempt on node2 is rejected with 'read-only transaction'.

evidence.requirement: Changes committed on the primary are visible on both standbys
evidence.summary: An INSERT executed on node1 (primary) appears in the repl_test table queried on both node2 and node3.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 31b01b46...; reboot acknowledged then connection dropped; post-restart boot_id 73effaec... (changed); postgresql active, not in recovery, both standbys reconnected streaming, firewall rule persisted; a post-restart INSERT on node1 replicated to node2 and node3.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id e31962a9...; reboot acknowledged then connection dropped; post-restart boot_id 57022f67... (changed); postgresql active, pg_is_in_recovery=true, repl_test data intact, and node1's pg_stat_replication shows node2 reconnected streaming.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 54bd1c3e...; reboot acknowledged then connection dropped; post-restart boot_id 3d9f50bd... (changed); postgresql active, pg_is_in_recovery=true, repl_test data intact, and node1's pg_stat_replication shows node3 reconnected streaming.
